what_its_for: Eluxadoline is used to treat irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D) in adults. It helps reduce belly pain and controls loose or frequent stools by working directly in your gut to slow things down and ease discomfort.
how_to_take: Take eluxadoline by mouth with food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Always take it with a meal or snack — taking it on an empty stomach may increase your risk of side effects. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet.
dosing: The usual dose is 100 mg taken twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening) with food. If you do not have a gallbladder, or if your doctor has concerns about certain side effects, they may lower your dose to 75 mg twice a day. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time with your next meal. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store eluxadoline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep the bottle tightly closed and store it out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking eluxadoline — even small amounts can raise the risk of serious pancreas problems. Avoid taking loperamide (Imodium) unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Avoid other medicines that slow your bowels unless your doctor approves. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking any new medications, vitamins, or supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: severe stomach pain (especially in the upper middle or upper right area), nausea or vomiting with stomach pain, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), severe constipation or no bowel movements for more than 4 days, chest pain, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your IBS-D symptoms are not improving after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Some people notice improvement in their diarrhea and belly pain within the first week of treatment. Full benefit may take a few weeks. Keep taking it as directed even if you feel better, and talk to your doctor if you do not see improvement after 4 weeks.
special_populations: Do NOT take eluxadoline if you do not have a gallbladder (it raises the risk of a serious pancreas problem), if you have a history of pancreatitis, severe liver disease, alcohol addiction or drink more than 3 alcoholic drinks per day, or if you have ongoing severe constipation or bowel blockage. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before taking this medicine. Safety in children has not been established — this medicine is only approved for adults.
